title: Find water
summary: Water runs downhill: check valley bottoms, the base of cliffs and dry stream beds.

list: Water runs downhill. Check valley bottoms, the base of cliffs, and dry stream beds; dig on the outside of bends where water last flowed.

blocks.cap: Water lingers longest under the outside of a bend, where the current cut deepest.

list: Signs of water nearby: green vegetation, swarming insects, animal trails that join up, and birds flying low and straight at dawn and dusk.
Catch rain with a tarp, poncho or large leaves.
Before sunrise, tie absorbent cloth around your ankles, walk through tall grass, and wring out the dew.
Tie a clear plastic bag over a leafy branch of a non-poisonous plant in full sun. Water collects in the bag as the leaves breathe.

blocks.cap: A transpiration bag yields a little water over several hours. Move it to a fresh branch daily.

list: Treat all wild water before drinking (see Make water safe).
